subject: Multiple Group IFA with items not common between groups

messages.author: e4c2f75e7fcb66ed
messages.subject: Multiple Group IFA with items not common between groups
parts:
Hi,

I have two different tests aimed at measuring two underlying factors, which correspond to two different facets of behaviour in children (externalising and internalising).

There are 6 items (X1-X6) that are in common to both tests, and I've already established partial measurement invariance using this subset. The syntax is something like:
                F1 =~ X1 + X2 + X3
                F2 =~ X4 + X5 + X6

However, I have more items in each test (Y1-Y10 in the first group, Z1-Z10 in the second group). Running separate-group EFA tells me that these load on the same two latent factors.

Is there a way that I can estimate a CFA model using the information from additional measures? This would be in a test-equating fashion, using, X1-X6 as anchors. In my dataset now Y1-Y10 are missing for the second group, and Z1-Z10 are missing for the first group.

I would like to run something with a syntax like:
                F1 =~       X1 + X2 + X3       + Y1 + Y2 + Y3 + Y4 + Y5        + Z1 + Z2 + Z3 + Z4 + Z5
                F2 =~       X4 + X5 + X6       + Y6 + Y7 + Y8 + Y9 + Y10      + Z6 + Z7 + Z8 + Z9 + Z10
Lavaan obviously tells me that there are missing entries in each group.

Do you have any suggestions?

Thanks!

Giacomo

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Multiple Group IFA with items not common between groups
parts: In my dataset now Y1-Y10 are missing for the second group, and Z1-Z10 are missing for the first group.

If you have different variables in different groups, I don't think the standard approach would work.  You could fit your model in more flexible Bayesian software, which would allow you to fit the model you want in each group.  The blavaan package makes the transition easy by translating lavaan syntax into JAGS syntax, which you can edit.  So you could try specifying a model with all variables in both groups, then when you save the JAGS file, you can edit that to have a subset of outcomes in each group. But if you are unfamiliar with the Bayesian approach, you will want to start with a lot of reading first.  Here is one introductory article, and Google can help you find more.

http://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/viewdoc/download?doi=10.1.1.310.3120&rep=rep1&type=pdf

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

Dear Johan,

Thanks for your help! I see your point here: constrain parameters in the group with no observations to zero.

I think the best way would be:
F1 =~ c(ax1,ax1)*X1 + c(ax2,ax2)*X2 + c(ax3,ax3)*X3 + c(ay11,0)*Y1 + c(ay21,0)*Y2 + c(ay31,0)*Y3 + c(ay41,0)*Y4 + c(ay51,0)*Y5
+ c(0,az12)*Z1 + c(0,az22)*Z2 + c(0,az32)*Z3 + c(0,az42)*Z4 + c(0,az52)*Z5
F2 =~ c(ax4,ax4)*X4 + c(ax5,ax5)*X5 + c(ax6,ax6)*X6 + c(ay61,0)*Y6 + c(ay71,0)*Y7 + c(ay81,0)*y8 + c(ay91,0)*Y9 + c(ay101,0)*Y10
+ c(0,az62)*Z6 + c(0,az72)*Z7 + c(0,az82)*Z8 + c(0,az92)*Z9 + c(0,az102)*Z10

Error in lav_samplestats_from_data(lavdata = lavdata, missing = lavoptions$missing,  :

In addition: Warning messages:
1: In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, group.label = group.label,  :

The items with zero loading should not actually feature in the likelihood, but I think this error is thrown before any calculations.

Any other ideas?

Giacomo

messages.author: 1b81d9050f0dbe89
messages.subject: Re: Multiple Group IFA with items not common between groups
parts:
You can run the following model

F1 =~ c(ax1,ax1)*X1 + c(ax2,ax2)*X2 + c(ax3,ax3)*X3 + c(ap11,ap12)*P1 + c(ap21,ap22)*P2 + c(ap31,ap32)*P3 + c(ap41,ap42)*P4 + c(ap51,ap52)*P5
F2 =~ c(ax4,ax4)*X4 + c(ax5,ax5)*X5 + c(ax6,ax6)*X6 + c(aq11,aq12)*Q1 + c(aq21,aq22)*Q2 + c(aq31,aq32)*Q3 + c(aq41,aq42)*Q4 + c(aq51,aq52)*Q5

where P1 <- rbind(Y1,Z1) etc and Q1 <- rbind(Y6,Z6) etc. Then you will not have missing values and should work out fine.

/Johan
